claims.title: Choosing a quadratic generator and the sign of the real coefficient
claims.hypotheses: A CM field E with x² = −d, d > 0, an embedding τ₀ and a finite set Q of rational primes at which −d is a local square.
claims.statement: One integral quadratic generator has split, separable polynomial at every locally split rational prime. A real coefficient c ≡ 1 modulo the product of Q is negative at the selected infinite place and positive at the others.

claims.title: A totally positive local generator of the codifferent
claims.hypotheses: The split polynomial at every prescribed prime and the trace codifferent of the ring of integers.
claims.statement: There is one totally positive element t′ of the codifferent which generates its localization at every prime ideal above the prescribed rational primes.

claims.title: One trace certificate for all prescribed primes
claims.hypotheses: The coefficients c and ω, a totally positive local codifferent generator, and the chosen embedding τ₀.
claims.statement: A purely imaginary δ has the required signs. A common integer coprime to all prescribed primes represents every scaled integral functional as a weighted trace and is divisible by c in the ring of integers.

claims.title: The perfect alternating form in arbitrary rank
claims.hypotheses: An arithmetic datum, a positive rank n and a scalar trace witness e coprime to the rational prime.
claims.statement: The standard alternating trace form on the rank-n lattice represents e³ times every integral functional and becomes perfect after localization at the prime.

claims.title: A common denominator for a fixed arithmetic datum
claims.hypotheses: Any fixed arithmetic datum with nonzero c and δ, its integral basis and the trace-integrality condition.
claims.statement: An explicit positive D makes the weighted trace perfect at every prime not dividing D. A datum constructed from x is good at each such prime where −d is a local square.
